headline: SECOND-BEST QUARTER EVER: GOLD MINERS HEAD INTO EARNINGS WITH $2,787/OZ PROFIT AND HISTORIC NAV DISCOUNTS
snippet: Adam Hamilton's July 11 earnings preview quantifies why gold miners are reporting near-record profits yet trading at historic discounts: Q2 2026 implied unit profits of $2,787/oz are the sector's second-best quarter on record (behind Q1's $3,129), yet the GDX top-25 P/E has collapsed from 49.6x to 20.2x during the January–July gold correction. Twelve consecutive quarters of year-over-year earnings growth, all-in sustaining costs averaging $1,703/oz against $4,100+ gold, and the Q2 reporting season beginning late July create the conditions under which each dollar of gold price recovery translates to $3–4 of EBITDA improvement — the maximum earnings leverage point in the current cycle.

headline: RARE EARTH SWEEP: ALL 18 TRACKED ELEMENTS UP IN JULY — GERMANIUM +27.8%, DYSPROSIUM +25.4%, TERBIUM +21.6%; ZERO DECLINES
snippet: The July 2026 rare earth market monthly report documents the broadest synchronized monthly price advance in the 2026 dataset: all 18 tracked rare earth elements rose in July with zero declines — a combination not seen in the prior 18 months of data. Germanium led at +27.8%, driven by Chinese export quota tightness and AI chip fabrication demand; dysprosium reversed sharply with +25.4% to $261.63/kg (its largest single-month move of the year); terbium cleared its previous 2026 high at $1,179.54/kg (+21.6%); and NdPr alloy rose to new 2026 highs. The structural driver is a second consecutive year of supply deficit against EV motor magnet and wind turbine generator demand, compounded by China's export licensing regime creating a five-to-one price disparity between ex-China and domestic prices for critical defence and clean energy elements.

headline: GR SILVER EXTENDS SAN MARCIAL 150m SOUTHEAST — 21.9m @ 168 g/t AG, 6.15m @ 447 g/t AG PUSHES BEYOND 2023 MRE BOUNDARY (TSXV:GRSL)
source_name: Investing News Network / GR Silver Mining Ltd.
snippet: GR Silver Mining Ltd. (TSXV: GRSL) announced July 10 that resource expansion drilling at the San Marcial area of the Plomosas Project in Sinaloa, Mexico confirmed a 150-metre southeastern extension of high-grade silver mineralisation beyond the 2023 NI 43-101 resource boundary — drill hole SMS26-07 returning 21.9 metres at 168 g/t silver including a 6.15-metre core at 447 g/t. A newly identified parallel breccia-hosted vein system (SMS26-02, SMS26-05, SMS26-08) represents additional mineralisation entirely outside the current resource model, making confirmed ore in both targets purely incremental to GR Silver's existing resource base at a time when $62/oz silver makes high-grade Mexican silver projects among the most economical in the sector.

headline: SILVER DEFENDS $60 FLOOR AHEAD OF CPI — SIXTH STRAIGHT GLOBAL DEFICIT YEAR, 46.3 MOZ SHORTFALL; INDUSTRIAL DEMAND COUNTERS FED PRESSURE
snippet: Silver has defended the $60.05 technical support level through a week of dollar strength and Fed hawkishness, with spot silver at $62 entering the July 14 CPI as the global market faces its sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit — the Silver Institute projecting a 46.3 million-ounce shortfall in 2026 against record total supply of approximately 1.05 billion ounces. Industrial demand from data centre power infrastructure, EV manufacturing, and electrification programmes is providing a demand floor that operates independently of investment sentiment; a soft CPI print that weakens the dollar could trigger a silver catch-up move toward $68–$72, given that silver's compressed short-to-long positioning ratio is at levels historically consistent with sharp short-covering acceleration.

headline: COPPER NEAR 2-WEEK LOW $6/LB — IRAN WAR DOLLAR SURGE CLOUDS GLOBAL MANUFACTURING; SULPHURIC ACID SHORTAGE ADDS REFINERY RISK
snippet: Copper futures pulled back toward the $6 per pound mark in mid-July 2026 — a two-week low — as the ongoing U.S.–Iran military conflict in the Persian Gulf drove the U.S. dollar higher and dampened expectations for global manufacturing demand, the primary driver of industrial copper consumption. A secondary supply-side complication emerged from the same conflict: a regional sulphuric acid shortage is affecting copper oxide leaching operations that depend on acid supply chains running through the Middle East, while Chile's Codelco posted an 18.3% year-on-year production decline. Chilean copper commission Cochilco raised its full-year 2026 forecast to $5.55/lb citing firm structural demand, but near-term price trajectory faces dollar headwinds until CPI resolves the macro direction.

headline: NGEX LUNAHUASI PHASE 4 COMPLETE: JUPITER ZONE HITS 18.84% CU OVER 7.6m — BONANZA CORE CONFIRMED AT LUNDIN GROUP PORPHYRY (TSX:NGEX)
snippet: NGEx Minerals Ltd. (TSX: NGEX) completed its 27,318-metre Phase 4 drill program at Lunahuasi in San Juan, Argentina on July 8, with best hole DPDH077 in the Jupiter zone returning 7.6 metres at 18.84% copper, 5.54 g/t gold and 336.7 g/t silver within a 10-metre interval at 0.88% Cu — confirming a bonanza-grade massive sulphide core within the porphyry system. The Saturn zone also extended, with DPDH072 returning 34 metres at 1.43% Cu, 1.8 g/t Au and DPDH069 confirming 135 metres at 1.18% Cu from 437 metres depth; the 18.84% Cu over 7.6m is among the highest copper grades reported at any modern porphyry copper discovery, establishing Lunahuasi as a world-class deposit advancing toward Prefeasibility.

headline: ANDINA COPPER CONFIRMS THIRD PIUQUENES PORPHYRY — 468m @ 0.50% CU FROM 700m DEPTH; NEW MIOCENE DISTRICT SYSTEM EMERGING (TSXV:ANDC)
snippet: Andina Copper Corp. (TSXV: ANDC) confirmed July 8 that drill hole PIU13 at the Piuquenes North target in San Juan, Argentina intersected 468 metres at 0.50% copper, 0.30 g/t gold and 3.04 g/t silver from 700 metres depth — including a 164-metre higher-grade core at 0.70% Cu, 0.44 g/t Au — making Piuquenes North the third distinct porphyry copper-gold system discovered within the emerging San Juan Miocene belt alongside Piuquenes East and the main Piuquenes zone. Only a fraction of the large magneto-telluric geophysical anomaly at Piuquenes North has been tested, and the next drill phase will target the full extent of what may be one of the largest untested porphyry copper systems identified anywhere in South America's Miocene belt during this exploration cycle.

headline: ISOENERGY STAKES 15.6% IN URANIUMX — HANDS 24.4M LB DIETER LAKE QUÉBEC URANIUM FOR BOARD SEAT AND 2% NSR ROYALTY (CSE:STMN)
snippet: IsoEnergy Ltd. (TSX: ISO) announced July 9 that subsidiary Consolidated Uranium Inc. has agreed to transfer its 100% interest in the Dieter Lake uranium project in north-central Québec — a historical resource of approximately 24.4 million pounds U₃O₈ traced over 6 km of strike — to UraniumX Discovery Corp. (CSE: STMN) in exchange for 18 million UraniumX shares plus a 2% net smelter returns royalty. IsoEnergy acquires a 15.6% strategic ownership stake with board nomination rights and anti-dilution protection, monetising a dormant non-core Québec asset while retaining full upside exposure through equity — a deal structure that reflects the increasing sophistication of how uranium senior developers are recycling non-priority land packages into optionality positions in focused junior operators.

headline: ATHA ENERGY OPENS NEW FRONT AT LAC 50 — 11.5m COMPOSITE URANIUM 4km ALONG STRIKE; SIXTH DISCOVERY IN 15 MONTHS IN ATHABASCA BASIN (TSXV:SASK)
snippet: ATHA Energy Corp. (TSXV: SASK) announced July 8 that the second drill hole at its new Lac 50 Northwest Discovery area — located 4 kilometres along strike from the known Lac 50 Deposit in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — intersected 11.5 metres of composite uranium mineralisation over five zones from 305 to 479.9 metres, including 1.6 metres of near-continuous high-grade uranium peaking at 40,162 counts per second. The result marks ATHA's sixth confirmed uranium discovery in 15 months of active exploration on a 100% hit rate across all regional exploration targets — extending the Lac 50 corridor's confirmed prospective strike to at least 4 kilometres and further validating the basement-hosted uranium model that has produced Cigar Lake and McArthur River, the world's highest-grade uranium mines.

headline: ROXMORE CONVERSE GOLD NEVADA: CV26-010C HITS 247.2m @ 0.51 g/t AU IN BATTLE MOUNTAIN TREND — BETTER-THAN-MODELLED GRADE IN INFERRED PIT (TSXV:RM)
source_name: The Prospector News / Roxmore Resources Corp.
snippet: Roxmore Resources Corp. (TSXV: RM) reported July 9 that drill hole CV26-010C at the Converse Gold Project on Nevada's Battle Mountain–Eureka Trend returned 247.2 metres at 0.51 g/t gold and 3.79 g/t silver, extending known mineralisation beyond the current pit shell boundary at better-than-modelled grades — the same geological corridor that hosts Barrick's Cortez complex and Nevada Gold Mines' operations. The Converse Phase 1 program continues with 30,000 metres planned and a second RC drill arriving in September; results confirming broader-than-modelled footprints at Carlin-corridor projects with existing NI 43-101 resources are the specific technical outcomes that support resource upgrades and attract PEA-level engineering.

headline: CHINA RARE EARTH PRICE INDEX HITS 271.9 — HIGHEST SINCE 2023 AS EXPORT LICENCE BACKLOG STRETCHES 60 DAYS FOR WESTERN BUYERS
snippet: China's official Rare Earth Price Index (REPI) has advanced to 271.9 — its highest reading since 2023 — as domestic and international supply of heavy rare earth elements including dysprosium, terbium, holmium and erbium remains structurally tight relative to demand from permanent magnet manufacturers and advanced materials producers. The REPI's advance reflects combined light and heavy REE strength: NdPr demand from EV motor magnets is driving light rare earth prices higher, while the Chinese export licensing regime has stretched approval timelines to 60-plus days for Western buyers — creating a bifurcated market where U.S. and European defence and clean energy manufacturers pay a substantial premium above Chinese domestic prices for the same critical materials.
